title: ambiguity
content_html:
ambiguity

A trace might be what remains, a faint amount, or a route we try to follow. A word or image can sustain several readings even when it is perfectly legible. In 3 symbols, the photographic and symbolic layers offer different ways to read the same image. Some ambiguities resolve with more context. Others are the reason we keep looking. Where does openness to several meanings meet uncertainty about evidence or a measured quantity? 3 symbols

Reading note. Existentialism. Simone de Beauvoir gives ambiguity a wider sense than a word with several meanings. We can act within circumstances we did not choose, and other people can experience our actions in ways we cannot control. A work takes on a similar openness when someone else takes it up and finds a meaning its maker could not foresee. The Ethics of Ambiguity, part I
